{"kind":"proof","text":"For each x∈[0,1), we have x^n→0, while f_n(1)=1 for every n. Thus the pointwise limit is

f(x)={0 if 0≤x<1, 1 if x=1}.

Assume that (f_n) converges uniformly. Since uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, its uniform limit must be f. Fix ε=1/4. For every N∈Z_+, take n=N and x=2^{-1/n}∈[0,1). Then f(x)=0, but

|f_n(x)−f(x)|=x^n=1/2>ε.

Hence no N can satisfy the uniform-convergence condition. Therefore (f_n) does not converge uniformly on [0,1].","reason":"The original proof does not first define the pointwise limit and does not fix a single positive ε witnessing failure of uniform convergence. The repaired proof supplies both points and directly negates the uniform-convergence criterion."}
